what_changed.text: Oil keeps falling — from $96 to $75. The Oil/SPR Capacity Ratio drops from 231 to 182, and the score finally steps down from 2 to 1. The acute price pressure has eased materially. The structural vulnerability — a reserve at 58% capacity with no political will to refill it — is still there, but at $75 the framework no longer flags it at maximum.

Gold cools to $4,382, with YoY decelerating from +44% to +29%. That pushes the Gold/Treasury Divergence indicator down to baseline for the first time this cycle: gold's annual pace has slowed while the 10Y ticked up to 4.47%. The framework's single most predictive signal has gone quiet — not reversed, quiet. Annual trends don't unwind in weeks, but the gap is no longer scoring.

S&P/Gold ratio climbs again, from 1.51 to 1.71, as equities extend their run and gold pulls back. Tier 3 holds at 3/12. Equities are reclaiming purchasing power in gold terms for a second consecutive reading — the framework records the move accurately rather than dismissing it.

Scores ease to T1=1/10, T2=5/20, T3=3/12. Status steps down from Emerging Disorder — Elevated to Emerging Disorder — Stable. The acute readings of April have relaxed: oil lower, gold cooler, the divergence at baseline. But the structural supply indicators — copper TC/RCs at $0, silver deficit at 800M oz — are still pinned at maximum. The phase hasn't changed. The temperature has.

contrarian: Oil fell to $75 and everyone called it the all-clear. The Canary isn't buying it. At $75, refilling the SPR to pre-2022 levels would still cost tens of billions and take years to execute. The 2022 release required drawing 180M barrels at $120 — that intervention stabilized markets temporarily. The reserve now sits at 415M barrels (58% capacity), and the political will to refill it doesn't exist at any price. The score eased from 2 to 1 because the acute price pressure lifted — not because the circuit breaker came back. A drop to $75 doesn't refill the reserve.

Gold pulled back to $4,382 and the consensus declared the trade over. But step back: gold is still up +29% over the year, and the dollar is hovering just below 100 at 99.7. The Gold/Treasury Divergence eased to baseline this reading — gold's annual pace slowed while yields ticked up — but a divergence going quiet after a +44% run is consolidation, not reversal. The framework reads the cooling honestly. It doesn't mistake a pause for a top.

The S&P 'recovered' against gold again. The ratio moved from 1.51 to 1.71. But zoom out: the S&P/Gold ratio peaked near 2.5 in late 2021. It now sits at 1.71 — meaning equities have surrendered roughly 30% of their purchasing power in gold terms over four years. Two good readings don't change the structural direction. The framework records them accurately. It doesn't change the interpretation.

divergence.description: The single most predictive indicator in The Canary. When gold surges and yields don't follow, the bond market is being artificially suppressed — either through direct purchases or implicit policy. This divergence preceded every major regime transition in the last 50 years.
divergence.current_reading: Current reading: Gold +29% YoY while 10Y yields are flat to slightly higher at 4.47%. The gap has narrowed enough that the Gold/Treasury Divergence indicator dropped to baseline this reading — the first time this cycle. That matters: this is the framework's core signal, and it has gone quiet. But quiet is not the same as resolved. Gold is still up sharply over the year, the dollar is hovering just below 100, and the multi-year divergence between gold and suppressed yields remains one of the widest in modern monetary history. The bond market is telling you everything is fine. The gold market and the dollar are no longer shouting — but they haven't changed their story.

consensus.wall_street: Supply normalization — OPEC+ responding, demand concerns easing. Energy price pressure is behind us.
consensus.atlas: The SPR is still at 58% capacity. The circuit breaker that worked in 2022 is still unavailable. The score eased from 2 to 1 because the acute price pressure lifted — but the indicator measures the underlying vulnerability, not the spot price, and that vulnerability remains.

consensus.wall_street: Dollar firming back toward 100 — the weakness was a blip. Reserve status intact.
consensus.atlas: Still below the 100 floor it broke earlier this cycle, with the 8-week trend up just +1.1%. A bounce inside a broken level isn't a recovery. Gold at $4,382 alongside a sub-100 dollar is still the monetary backdrop the framework watches — the urgency has eased, the setup hasn't.

consensus.wall_street: S&P at 7,511 confirms the bull market is intact. Gold was the overreaction.
consensus.atlas: S&P/Gold at 1.71 vs the 2021 peak of ~2.5. Equities are up nominally, but down ~30% in gold terms over 4 years. Two readings of outperformance are recorded accurately by the framework — they don't change the 4-year trend.
Balance sheet still growing — +1.0% over 3 months — at a $40B/mo purchase pace. Direction matters more than rate level. The stealth expansion continues, even as the pace cools.

consensus.wall_street: Baa at 2.47% is historically normal — no stress
consensus.atlas: Ticked up from 2.40% to 2.47%. Still well inside normal, but the direction is the wrong way. Watch whether this drifts wider over the next few readings.
TC/RCs at $0 says smelters are in crisis. Headline inventory masks geographic dislocation and tariff front-loading.

positioning.intro: The status steps down to Emerging Disorder — Stable. Oil fell to $75, gold cooled to +29% YoY, and the Gold/Treasury Divergence dropped to baseline — the acute April readings have relaxed across Tier 1. The framework records this honestly: short-term mean reversion is real and worth tracking. But the structural indicators haven't moved — copper smelters are still paying miners, silver deficits are compounding, and the Fed's balance sheet is still growing. The temperature has come down; the phase has not. Position for the structure, not the noise.

posture.label: Gold — overweight
posture.reason: Pulled back to $4,382, +29% YoY with 8-week momentum negative at -7.4%. The annual trend has cooled and the Gold/Treasury Divergence eased to baseline this reading — gold is consolidating, not breaking. The structural case (dollar below 100, Fed still expanding) is intact; the tactical setup has softened. A pause after a +44% run is normal.

posture.label: Bitcoin — overweight
posture.reason: Functions as high-beta gold in monetary regime transitions. The same backdrop — a sub-100 dollar and a Fed still buying — is the setup BTC correlates with most strongly. Position size for volatility, especially while gold consolidates.

posture.label: Short-term Treasuries — hold
posture.reason: T-bills under 1-year maturity. Dry powder for deployment if the coiling pattern breaks toward escalation. Eliminated at Crisis Acceleration when Treasuries themselves become the problem.

posture.label: Critical materials — overweight
posture.reason: Copper TC/RCs still at $0 (score 2) and silver deficit at 800M oz cumulative (score 2) — both supply-side indicators pinned at maximum. Oil/SPR eased to a score of 1 as crude fell to $75, but the reserve is still at 58% capacity. The structural shortages are unmoved by the price pullback.

posture.label: Equities — underweight
posture.reason: S&P/Gold ratio rose to 1.71 from the 1.40 low — the framework records this. But the 4-year trend shows equities have lost ~30% of their purchasing power in gold terms since 2021. Nominal gains masking real losses.

posture.label: Long Treasuries — underweight
posture.reason: Yields ticked up to 4.47% but remain structurally suppressed against a Fed that is still buying. With the dollar hovering below 100, the case for long-duration bonds remains weak even as the acute divergence eases.

escalation: Gold 8-week momentum recovers above +10% → Gold Momentum returns to Score 2 and Tier 1 re-escalates. Currently at -7.4% — the window has widened as gold consolidates.

Fed shifts to long-duration purchases while The Canary reads Early Warning or above → immediate Crisis Acceleration (Override Rule #4). QE launched from Stable does not trigger — it's a crisis response, not a cause.
Treasury auction B/C drops below 2.0 → demand crisis signal. Currently masked by Fed purchases — watch what happens if they pause.
Tier 2 confirming score reaches ≥8 → triggers Transition via combined T1+T2 gate. Currently at 5/20. If credit spreads keep drifting wider or foreign holdings drop, the path to 8 shortens.
deescalation: Gold YoY drops below +30% while yields rise → genuine tightening. Currently at +29% — just crossed below the threshold, but yields are flat rather than rising, so this reads as gold cooling, not genuine tightening.
Fed resumes QT at full pace → balance sheet contracting. Not just slowing purchases — actively shrinking. Balance sheet is still growing, though the pace has cooled to +1.0% over 3 months.
Tier 1 drops to 0–2 (currently 1/10) → returns to Stable. Tier 1 is now at 1/10 — this condition is met, which is what pulled the status down to Stable.
Deficit/GDP falls below 5% → structural fiscal pressure easing. Currently at 5.8% and rising.

track_record.intro: Applied retroactively across nine historical periods, The Canary identified every major regime transition 3–6 months early with near-zero false positives.

adversarial.label: Gold rally (+25%)
adversarial.result: No signal ✔ — cyclical bounce with no yield divergence or Fed expansion. Gold reversed within a year.

adversarial.label: Gold bear market (−45%)
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — real tightening with rising yields. The system correctly read this as non-monetary.

adversarial.label: Fed tightening cycle
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — QT was running and balance sheet shrinking. No divergence to trigger on.

adversarial.label: LTCM / Russia crisis
adversarial.result: Correctly filtered ✔ — financial stress but no monetary regime implications. Fed cut rates and markets stabilized.

adversarial.label: SVB banking stress
adversarial.result: Brief signal, self-corrected ✔ — initial spike in Fed lending resolved within weeks. No sustained monetary shift.

adversarial.label: 30-year balance sheet expansion
adversarial.result: Right on direction, open on timing — BOJ's experiment is still running. The framework flags the trajectory correctly but can't call the endpoint.
